models.confirmed_production_model: ExtraTrees is the production classifier. Confirmed by the capstone team, and it is what the capstone report documents. Corroborated in code by the config.py default, its comment ('The current production artifact is an sklearn ExtraTreesClassifier'), and the assertion in tests/test_fall_detector.py. Note that the development machine's .env pointed at the superseded XGBoost behavior.joblib instead, so the capstone demo ran that model rather than this one; see the superseded section below.

superseded.purpose: An older XGBoost behavior classifier. Its filename is now reused by the final ExtraTrees model above, so identify it by checksum and size, never by name.
superseded.warning: Accepts the same 141 features and returns the same 3 classes as the current model, so it loads and runs silently if a config or .env points at it. It is not the current model. Listed here only so the file can be identified by checksum if it is found on a machine.

superseded.purpose: Legacy portable XGBoost artifact, used only when the primary behavior file is absent.
superseded.status: Not present in the repository, in git history at this commit, or on the development machine. Deleted from git in f1f2b90. No checksum can be recorded.
superseded.warning: Because it is a fallback, a missing primary file does not fail loudly if this file ever reappears. Do not supply it unless there is a reason to.

accelerated_optional.note: TensorRT engines and their ONNX intermediates, built from the .pt files above by backend/scripts/export_tensorrt.py. Optional in the sense that the system runs correctly without them and nothing loads one automatically - a setting must point at the .engine path explicitly - but see reference_configuration: the demonstrated system did point at them. No reid engine exists; export_tensorrt.py covers PPE, pose and sign only.
accelerated_optional.portability_warning: A TensorRT engine is tied to the GPU compute capability, driver and TensorRT version that built it, and fails to deserialize at startup anywhere else. If De Heus hardware differs from build_environment below, these files will not load and are not a defect — rebuild them with scripts/export_tensorrt.py on the target machine. The .pt files remain the source of truth.

build_environment.profile_note: The optimisation profile is tuned for the live shape (1280x720 letterboxing to 384x640) and capped at 640x640, sized for a 6 GB card. A larger card would benefit from rebuilding rather than reusing these.

files.loaded_by: MODEL_PATH (set it to weights/ppe.engine to use)
FALL_MODEL_PATH (set it to weights/pose.engine to use)
files.note: Built with a batch size matching BEHAVIOR_BATCH_MAX_SIZE; changing that setting requires a rebuild.

files.loaded_by: SIGN_MODEL_PATH (set it to weights/sign.engine to use)

files.note: Export intermediate. Only needed to rebuild an engine without re-exporting from the .pt.

accelerated_optional.obtain_from: Delivered separately, outside this repository, by the member of the capstone team who also maintains the ppe_labeling labelling-tool documentation. De Heus contact: Ethan Phuc (Nguyen Trong Phuc), Information Technology, ethan.phuc@deheus.com
accelerated_optional.reference_configuration: The capstone development and demo machine ran PPE, sign and pose inference from these engines, not from the .pt files: MODEL_PATH=weights/ppe.engine, SIGN_MODEL_PATH=weights/sign.engine, FALL_MODEL_PATH=weights/pose.engine. Only FALL_REID_MODEL_PATH stayed at weights/reid.pt, because no reid engine is built. Any demonstrated performance was therefore TensorRT performance. Running from .pt is supported and was verified on a CPU-only clean install, but is slower.
